stg_001: You can recognise them by the pair facing each other across the square, each trunk over 4.7 metres round. They stand in Place de la Republique.
stg_002: You can recognise them by the pair standing together on the spot of the vanished chateau's entrance gate. They stand in Parc Schulmeister, Place de la Meinau.
stg_003: You can recognise it by standing at the centre of the park, roughly 40 metres tall, impossible to walk past without noticing. It stands in Parc du Contades.
stg_004: You can recognise it by its trunk, over 5 metres round, unusually large for a tree squeezed onto old-town paving. It stands in the Place du marche aux poissons.
stg_005: You can recognise it by its trunk, about 4.5 metres round, shading a cafe terrace on the quay. It stands on the Quai de la Bruche, Petite France.
stg_006: You can recognise it by its wide, low-spreading crown, unusual for a beech, and roots running over the surface like cables. It stands in the Parc de l'Orangerie.
stg_007: You can recognise it by its dark purple leaves, almost translucent red when they open in late spring. It stands in Place de l'Universite, before the Palais Universitaire.
stg_008: You can recognise it by its grey-blue needles, reading almost metallic in flat light, held all year round. It stands in the grounds of the Centre administratif.
